problem:
The polar equation of the circle that is centered at the origin and that passes through the point $A(6,2)$ is$\,\,r=$
{{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
A circle of radius $k$ centered at the origin has the polar equation $r=k.$

We can compute the radius $k$ of our circle using the Pythagorean theorem, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}k & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{6}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36+4} \\  & =\sqrt{40} \\  & =2\sqrt{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the circle is $r=2\sqrt{10}.$
